voice.stance: The navigator's voice. Every ATLAS sentence orients: place, direction, distance, exception. The reader is somewhere on the line and wants to know what lies ahead. A sentence with no location is cargo with no waybill, and it does not belong on the page.
voice.title_grammar: Place first, then status, then the exception.
voice.title_example: KP 812 to 840: three crossings pending, corridor clear

do.rule: Lead with the place: chainage, section, or site.
do.why: Geography drives the layout in this language, so it drives the syntax too.

do.rule: Use movement verbs: advances, reaches, holds at.
do.why: A route report is about motion, and static verbs hide the trend.
Two delayed crossings mean nothing until the reader knows where they are.

dont.why: If it has no coordinates it is not route news.
Ahead and behind mean nothing on a line until you say which way.

dont.rule: No place named in the text that the map does not show.
dont.why: Text and map anchor each other one to one.

contrast.generic: Good progress is being made along the route with teams working hard to maintain momentum.
contrast.voiced: Lowering-in reached KP 796, 18 km short of the coastal tie-in. Two wet crossings at KP 802 hold the front.
